Documentation

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com

Guides for every XRef workflow, generated from the Markdown in the repository. Start with the command reference on the home page, or the recorded Live Analysis walkthrough.

Search

xref refs

Find every instruction and data slot that names an address or a piece of text. It is the usual first step on a stripped binary: start from a string you can see in the program's output, find the code that uses it, then read that code with c or asm.

xref istr

Find strings that a function builds from immediate stores instead of reading them from .rodata: compilers write short strings with movabs / mov [mem], imm instructions, so a text search of the data sections misses them. istr TEXT is the same search as refs --inline TEXT.

xref imm

Instructions with an immediate operand.

xref disp

Instructions reading or writing struct fields: non-stack memory operands with these displacements.

xref find

Functions satisfying multiple predicates in one parallel pass.

xref sym

List function symbols whose name contains a pattern. Useful only on binaries that still carry a symbol table; stripped release binaries have none (use refs, where or find there).

xref field

Recover the in-memory layout behind serialized keys. Give field the keys a program prints (JSON object keys, for example) and it finds the serializer code that emits them, the offset of each field relative to the serialized value, and, with --write, candidate code that writes those fields.

xref data

Read typed values at a virtual address of the binary: the address is mapped through the load segments (ELF PT_LOAD, Mach-O segments) and each element is printed with its address. Use it when pseudo-C or assembly loads from a constant address (a table indexed by some value, a string, a constant) and

Functions

xref stats

Functions, code size, data pointers, imports and panic locations.

xref deps

List what a binary says about how it was built: the dependency manifest Rust's cargo-auditable embeds in .dep-v0, or the module list Go embeds in .go.buildinfo, together with the compiler and linker strings from .comment and the GNU Build-ID (or Mach-O LC_UUID). Use it to see which crates or modules

xref func

The function (exact .eh_frame range) containing each address.

xref card

A one-screen summary of a function: which argument registers and stack slots it reads, its return registers, the fields it stores to (grouped by base), every call with its decoded arguments, indirect calls, panic paths and exits. Use it to decide whether a function is worth reading in full with c.

xref c

Decompile functions to structured, typed pseudo-C. c lifts the machine code of each function containing the given addresses: arguments, local variables, loops and branches, calls with their constant arguments, and string literals.

xref asm

Annotated disassembly of the function containing an address.

xref slice

Backward program slice: minimal pseudo-C statements and branches reaching a target address or text.

xref layout

Reconstructed struct field layout accessed via an argument register (and optionally callees receiving it).

xref dump

Parallel modular pseudo-C dump grouped by recovered Rust source paths (<OUT>/crate/src/mod.c).

Call graph

xref callers

Direct calls and jumps to an address, and code taking its address or loading a slot holding it.

xref calls

Calls and tail jumps of the function containing an address, in code order.

xref table

Fixed-size records from an address, each 8-byte field with what fills it: a relocated pointer to a function, an import or data, or the file's bytes.

xref args

Constant and symbolic arguments at every call site of a function (rdi..r9 and stack0..N).

xref callargs

Every call site in the binary that passes a given constant as an argument, grouped by callee.

xref path

Shortest call chains from function FROM to function TO over direct calls, tail jumps and pointer slots.

xref tree

Indented caller or callee tree of a function, with ranges and first panic locations.

Rust source & enums

xref where

Functions passing source locations whose file contains a pattern (and optionally at one line).

xref src

Rust source locations (panic Locations) the function containing an address passes.

xref files

Distinct source files of the panic locations (optionally containing a pattern), with counts.

xref error

Enum variant whose Display/match arm names a text: the jump-table index of the referencing arm.

xref origin

From an error message to the code that builds it: the stores of the message's enum tag, with the conditions that guard each.

xref variant

Jump-table arms of the function containing an address for enum variant indices, with the texts they name.

xref arm

Jump-table indices whose arm holds each address (closest preceding arm of every table, best first).

Across builds

xref match

Counterpart of each function in another build of the binary, scored by shared locations, strings, immediates and call graph.

xref diff-c

Normalized cross-build pseudo-C diff between counterpart functions in two binaries.

Live process

xref live maps

Show the memory map of a running Linux process and check it against the binary passed with -b: the executable must be the one that is running (compared by SHA-256), and xref computes the PIE slide that links runtime addresses to static ones. Every other live command starts with the same check. Linux

xref live resolve

Translate addresses between the binary on disk and a running process: a static address (as printed by every static command) becomes the runtime address in this process, and a runtime address (from a debugger, a crash log, perf) becomes the static one. The translation uses the verified PIE slide and

xref live memscan

Search a running process for a known value: xref scans its private writable memory (rw-p: heap, anonymous mappings, writable data) for consecutive little-endian u64 values and prints the words around each hit. Use it to locate a structure you know a field of, then resolve the pointers next to it wit

xref live probe

Count how often code runs in a live process, and who calls it: xref attaches uprobes to static code addresses (translated through the verified PIE slide), counts hits per probe, and with --callers recovers each caller's return address from .eh_frame and checks that it follows a call instruction.

xref live trace

Record what a thread does between two points: each time a thread enters a --start function, xref opens a window for that thread and records, in order, the entries and returns of the traced functions until the window closes (--stop-return of the start function, or --stop at an address). --callees-of

xref live watch

Catch the instruction that writes a field: xref sets x86 hardware data watchpoints (DR0–DR3, up to four addresses of 1–8 bytes) on a running process and attributes every store to its instruction, function and static address. --follow re-arms the watch when a pointer-backed buffer moves (for example

xref live profile

Sample where a running process spends its CPU time and save a bounded recording (.xprof) that the profile commands read: hot functions, blocks and instructions, with call chains unwound from .eh_frame (--callers dwarf, the default). Recording can be limited to a function (--within) or to windows ope

Profiles & stacks

xref profile report

Summarize a recorded profile (.xprof, from live profile or profile import): the hottest functions, basic blocks, source lines, caller paths or instructions, with self and total shares.

xref profile annotate

Show where inside one function the samples fell: its disassembly (or pseudo-C with --c) with each line's share of the function and of the whole profile.

xref profile diff

Compare two profiles by sample share: which functions got hotter or cooler. Two recordings of the same binary are compared function by function; with --other NEW_BINARY the second profile is of another build, and functions are paired with match (heuristic, and marked as such).

xref profile import

Convert a profile recorded by Linux perf (perf.data or perf script text) into an .xprof recording that the profile commands read. The target's runtime mapping comes from a saved /proc/<pid>/maps (--maps with --pid) or a base address (--base).

xref symbolize

Map addresses from a saved run onto the selected executable: plain address lists, perf script call chains or folded stacks. It never attaches to a process. Frames outside the executable, in shared libraries, in an ambiguous mapping or in a range without unwind information stay explicitly unresolved.

xref edges

Import observed caller → callee adjacencies from saved stacks (address lists, perf script call chains, folded stacks) into an evidence store that graph queries use when asked to. Static call graphs miss calls through pointers; observed stacks fill some of them in. Counts are stack samples, not call

Machine interfaces

xref query

Run one versioned JSON query and print a JSON response. This is the same interface the MCP server exposes, for scripts and agents that prefer one process per question. Operations: info (with first-contact triage), strings, refs, function, calls, callers, call_context, investigate, field_origin, symb

xref mcp

Serve a read-only MCP server over stdio for one binary. An agent (Claude Code, Codex, any MCP client) gets the xref_query tool with the same operations as query, against one immutable image identified by its SHA-256. With --allow-live-pid PID it also gets the opt-in xref_live tool, pinned to that ve
